The gate of M1 is wired to `iout` instead of `iin`, so the reference device is not diode-connected. With its gate on the output node, which carries almost no current, M1 cannot set a gate voltage for M2. The measurements agree: `vin_node` is 0.02 V, so the input node sinks rather than being biased near threshold, and `iout` is 2.4 pA, far below 20 µA. The 100 % error and the compliance and rout results (which are meaningless with M2 off) follow from this.

M2 is wired correctly (drain `iout`, gate `iin`), and the 19.28/20.23 width ratio is a plausible nominal sizing. The only other device is M2, so the second entry is a weaker candidate, and there is no third element.
